description: Fix a heapq-based priority queue that breaks ties by comparing the payload itself (crashing on incomparable payloads) into a FIFO-stable one
prompts: pq.py's StablePriorityQueue pushes plain (priority, item) tuples onto a heap. When two items share a priority, heapq falls back to comparing the ITEMS directly - which raises TypeError for items that aren't comparable (e.g. plain dicts), and even when it doesn't raise, it has nothing to do with insertion order. Fix push/pop so that: (1) items with a lower priority number come out first, (2) items with EQUAL priority come out in the order they were pushed (FIFO), and (3) items never need to be compared to each other directly - arbitrary non-comparable payloads (dicts, custom objects) must work.

test_setup_files.test_pq_hidden.py:
from pq import StablePriorityQueue


def test_priority_order():
    q = StablePriorityQueue()
    q.push(5, 'low')
    q.push(1, 'high')
    q.push(3, 'mid')
    assert [q.pop(), q.pop(), q.pop()] == ['high', 'mid', 'low']


def test_equal_priority_is_fifo():
    q = StablePriorityQueue()
    q.push(1, 'first')
    q.push(1, 'second')
    q.push(1, 'third')
    assert [q.pop(), q.pop(), q.pop()] == ['first', 'second', 'third']


def test_incomparable_payloads_do_not_raise():
    q = StablePriorityQueue()
    q.push(1, {'id': 1})
    q.push(1, {'id': 2})
    assert q.pop() == {'id': 1}
    assert q.pop() == {'id': 2}
